title: NSI, A.1 LLC v. City of Springfield (Developer Sues to Block Data Center Moratorium After Relying on City's Own Zoning Sign-Off)
jurisdiction: Circuit Court of Greene County, Missouri
amount: Not a monetary damages claim; developer seeks declaratory and injunctive relief blocking enforcement of a 120-day data center moratorium against a project it says the city already approved in writing
summary: Missouri developer Trent Overhue, through NSI, A.1 LLC, sued the City of Springfield on September 17, 2026 in Greene County Circuit Court, seeking to block a 120-day data center moratorium the city adopted June 29, 2026 from applying to his project. The six-count petition alleges the city had twice issued written zoning verification permitting a basement data-processing center at the site under its PD 251 planned-development zoning, and that the moratorium was adopted without the plan-commission review, public hearing, and Sunshine Law notice a genuine zoning change requires.
significance: Tests whether a municipality can retreat from its own written zoning verification through a moratorium adopted outside normal zoning-amendment procedure, a question with direct relevance to any developer who has incurred predevelopment costs in reliance on a jurisdiction's own sign-off. The case is one of three concurrent Missouri data center disputes, signaling that local moratoria adopted hastily in response to AI-driven data center demand carry real procedural litigation risk.
